title: Suggestions for review - nothing here is implemented; a reviewer picks a path first
workflow: 1) reviewer reads the suggestion, its options and what each costs; 2) reviewer writes a verdict (option letter, or 'reject'); 3) only then does a session implement it. This namespace implements none of them; each is a proposal with a measurable clearing condition.
verdict_rule: verdict is blank on every row by design. A non-blank verdict is the only thing that turns a suggestion into work.

rows.title: Buy, or formally decline, a price feed
rows.why: Three whole requirement families (snapshot store, residual/CLV, vig decomposition) are blocked by one missing input. Every session so far has worked around it with blanks; the blanks are correct but they are not a plan.

options.text: license a historical+live odds feed and make price capture the project's first ingestion duty
decline prices permanently: publish fair lines and availability indices only, with no residual column anywhere
keep third-party archive captures, labelled third-party on every row, and forbid the word 'market' from a leaderboard title

rows.cost: A: money + a new collector; B: nothing, but rewards stay unpayable; C: labelling discipline only

rows.title: Turn the manual capture into a scheduled collector with a hash chain
rows.why: The whole 'delta not level' argument rests on dated captures. This session produced one; six dated renders exist in the repo only because six separate agent sessions happened to read the page on different days. That is not cadence, it is luck.

options.text: a GitHub Actions workflow on a Wed/Thu/Fri + daily-to-kickoff cron that commits a dated capture with sha256 and runs engine/drift.py
keep manual capture, but make drift.py's expectations the release gate so an unnoticed change cannot publish
do nothing and accept single-week captures as the ceiling of every availability feature

rows.cost: A: one workflow + storage decision; B: none, file already written; C: the availability roadmap stalls

rows.title: Write the game-book parser before writing another model
rows.why: 'Who actually started' is the only field that turns the availability graph from a one-sided list into a testable claim, and the official PDF link is already published per fixture. Nobody in this repo parses it.

options.text: parse participation lists for one full week (14 fixtures), store as a dated dataset, publish coverage per club
parse one club one week as a spike, then decide
skip game books and accept that the availability graph stays one-sided

rows.cost: A: one parser + PDF handling in CI; B: half a day; C: R-10 and R-25 stay blocked forever

rows.title: Publish provisional-but-unranked rows instead of an empty leaderboard
rows.why: A board that shows nothing invites someone to 'fix' it with a 77-game win rate. Showing the rows with an explicit 'not ranked - n below the floor' band protects both the sample discipline and the reader's patience.

options.text: add a 'provisional, unranked' band with n, the floor and the reason
keep the board empty until qualification
show ranks in grey with a warning (weakest option: still reads as a ranking)

rows.title: Make the transactions hub a first-class feed, joined to every availability row
rows.why: The one hard conflict this session caught (a traded player still on his old club's report) is exactly what a versioned roster event prevents. The official hub and dated trade tracker already exist.

options.text: daily transaction-hub capture, keyed to club+player, invalidating any depth or availability row older than the last event
weekly reconciliation only, accepting up to 6 days of stale rows
no join; document staleness as a permanent caveat

rows.cost: A: one collector + a staleness rule; B: a script; C: nothing

rows.title: Ship the removal-of-luck panel with only the components that are computable, and name the missing ones on the panel
rows.why: Two components (opponent adjustment, league base rates) are computable from the official standings arithmetic; two (CLV, ROI) cannot exist without prices. A panel that says '2 of 4 live, 2 blocked by DEC-P1' is more useful than an empty box.

options.text: ship 2-of-4 with the blockers stated on the panel
withhold until all four exist
substitute a proxy (e.g. rest-day imbalance) and label it a proxy

rows.cost: display work; C needs a written proxy definition

rows.title: State the repo's negative pricing result on the landing page, not in an appendix
rows.why: The published walk-forward comparison says our lines are worse than the market's on the graded sample. Hiding that is how a project loses trust in its own dashboard.

options.text: headline it on the landing page next to the readiness counts
keep it on the peer namespace's page and link once
re-run it first with the new corpus definition, then publish

rows.cost: A/B: none; C: a re-run, and the re-run needs prices to be comparable

rows.title: Collapse the 22 NFL namespaces to one canonical site with appendices
rows.why: The same requirement is met 22 times with different table shapes. A reviewer cannot compare 22 dashboards, and 'which number is the number' becomes its own question.

options.text: declare one canonical namespace, freeze the others as read-only appendices with a banner
build an index-of-indexes that reports each namespace's row counts side by side (this session's repo-review page is a first version)
leave it; accept duplicate work forever

rows.cost: A: a rename + links; B: nothing more, it exists; C: hidden cost each session

rows.title: Add a coverage column to every dataset on the site
rows.why: Three captures of one official page differ by 21, 71 and 0 rows. Without a published coverage number (rows, sections, designation coverage) a reader cannot tell a small week from a bad parse.

options.text: coverage line under every table, generated from the data, not typed
coverage only on the availability page
nothing; rely on flags

rows.cost: A: generator change; B: smaller change; C: none

rows.title: Freeze the ablation protocol now, run it when the data exists
rows.why: 'Ablations not fixed penalties' is the right method, and it is currently unrunnable (needs >=2 dated availability weeks). The mistake to avoid is inventing the comparison after seeing the result.

options.text: commit the protocol (arms, holdout, uncertainty, reporting) as a pre-registration now
wait and design it when data exists (risk: design follows result)
run a fixed-penalty version meanwhile, marked non-comparable

rows.cost: A: one file; C: risks the exact defect the brief bans

rows.title: Re-scope the depth requirements that depend on a source that does not exist
rows.why: Four requirements (rank groups, shared/empty slots, two parse failures, the deficiency matrix) all assume a depth dataset that neither this repo nor nfl.com provides. Left as-is they will be 'delivered' by inventing ranks.

options.text: mark them blocked-with-source-requested and re-scope to snap-share from game books if SUG-03 succeeds
license a depth-chart feed
drop them and record the drop

rows.cost: A: a status change; B: money; C: owner sign-off

rows.title: Publish the read-window and the imprecision, always
rows.why: The fetch path used here does not return page bytes or a per-call clock. Storing a fake minute-level timestamp would make the ledger look precise and be wrong. This session recorded a bracketed window with the reason; that convention should become the site rule.

options.text: adopt 'read window + method + limitation' as the required capture header on every dataset
keep per-file dates only
invest in a byte-level capture path so real hashes and exact times are possible

rows.cost: A: a convention; C: an infrastructure change
